title: Attorney General Nessel warns Michigan residents about post-storm scams after recent flooding
text:
Michigan Attorney General Dana Nessel reminded residents on April 15 to be cautious of post-storm scams as communities recover from recent severe storms and rising floodwaters. Governor Gretchen Whitmer has extended the activation of the State Emergency Operations Center, with officials urging caution in flooded areas and adherence to emergency orders.
The warning comes as many homeowners seek quick repairs, a situation that can lead to hasty decisions and vulnerability to fraud. The State of Michigan has provided resources on the MIREADY website for recovery steps, along with a new site for updates on dam impacts and statewide flooding.
“As communities across Michigan face flood warnings and watches, residents must be prepared,” said Attorney General Nessel. “If you live near a flood zone, monitor official updates and sign up for local alerts. Unfortunately, severe weather and flooding often bring out bad actors looking to profit from impacted residents. Before making any repairs, remember to do your homework and know your rights.”
Nessel reissued four consumer alerts covering disaster-related scams, towing laws, risks when buying flood-damaged vehicles, and tips for researching home repair contractors. She advised residents not to rush into agreements or payments before verifying credentials: “Breathe! Take some time to process what has happened… Legitimate home repair contractors understand you need time to do your homework…” Other tips include reviewing insurance policies carefully before committing funds for repairs.
Residents are encouraged not to pay in full upfront or use cash payments; instead they should ensure all agreements are documented in writing. Credit card payments offer additional protections if disputes arise over incomplete work.
According to the official website , the Michigan Department of Attorney General advances social efforts through actions against human trafficking and support for vulnerable populations. The department also focuses on serving state residents through public service initiatives according to its official website . Dana Nessel is recognized as Michigan’s 54th attorney general according to state records . The department operates with statewide authority designed specifically for resident protection as stated by the agency .
In addition, the office influenced policy by drafting the Clean Slate law in 2019 which expanded expungement opportunities according to their official account .
Nessel urged those seeking more information or wishing to file complaints about suspected scams following disasters or storms contact her Consumer Protection Team using available phone numbers or online forms.
